events.name: Neolithic settlement at Mehrgarh
events.summary: Early farming settlement in Baluchistan with evidence of cultivated barley and wheat and domesticated animals.
events.note: Earliest levels dated c. 7000-6000 BCE depending on source.

events.name: Excavation of Harappa begins
events.summary: Excavations at Harappa bring the Harappan (Indus) civilisation to light.

events.name: Excavation of Mohenjo-daro begins
events.summary: R.D. Banerji begins work at Mohenjo-daro.

events.name: Mature Harappan phase
events.summary: Urban phase with planned cities, standardised weights and the Indus script.
events.note: Textbook ranges vary (e.g. c. 2600-1900 or 2500-1750 BCE).

events.name: Decline of Harappan urbanism
events.summary: De-urbanisation of the major Harappan sites; causes are debated.

events.name: Early (Rig) Vedic period
events.summary: Period of composition of most of the Rig Veda; largely pastoral society in the Sapta Sindhu region.
events.note: Chronology is debated.

events.name: Later Vedic period
events.summary: Expansion into the Ganga plains, use of iron, settled agriculture and sharper varna divisions.

events.name: Age of the sixteen Mahajanapadas
events.summary: Territorial states such as Magadha, Kosala, Vatsa and Avanti emerge in north India.

events.name: Achaemenid control of Gandhara
events.summary: Gandhara and the Indus region appear as provinces of the Persian Achaemenid empire.

events.name: Life of Gautama Buddha (traditional dates)
events.summary: Founder of Buddhism.
events.note: Many historians now place his death c. 400 BCE (short chronology).

events.name: Life of Vardhamana Mahavira
events.summary: Twenty-fourth Jain tirthankara.
events.note: Jain tradition gives 599-527 BCE.

events.name: Reign of Bimbisara of Magadha
events.summary: Haryanka ruler who expanded Magadha by conquest (Anga) and marriage alliances.
events.note: Traditional dates tied to the Buddha's chronology.

events.name: First Buddhist Council at Rajagriha
events.summary: Held soon after the Buddha's death to compile his teachings.
events.note: Date depends on the Buddha's death date.

events.name: Alexander's campaign in north-west India
events.summary: Macedonian campaign in the north-west; the army refused to go beyond the Beas.

events.name: Battle of the Hydaspes (Jhelum)
events.summary: Alexander defeats Porus and reinstates him as ruler.

events.name: Chandragupta Maurya founds the Mauryan empire
events.summary: Chandragupta overthrows the Nandas.
events.note: Dates range c. 324-321 BCE.

events.name: War and treaty with Seleucus Nicator
events.summary: Seleucus cedes north-western territories; Megasthenes later comes as envoy to Pataliputra.

events.name: Accession of Ashoka
events.summary: Ashoka succeeds Bindusara.
events.note: Accession dated c. 273-268 BCE in different works.

events.name: Kalinga War
events.summary: Conquest of Kalinga; Rock Edict XIII records Ashoka's remorse and turn to dhamma.
events.note: Eighth year after Ashoka's consecration.

events.name: Third Buddhist Council at Pataliputra
events.summary: Held under Ashoka; followed by missions to spread Buddhism.
events.note: Known mainly from Sri Lankan chronicles.

events.name: End of the Mauryan dynasty
events.summary: Pushyamitra Shunga kills the last Maurya ruler and founds the Shunga dynasty.

events.name: James Prinsep deciphers Brahmi
events.summary: Decipherment that made Ashoka's edicts readable.

events.name: Indo-Greek king Menander (Milinda)
events.summary: Best-known Indo-Greek ruler; his dialogue with Nagasena is the Milindapanha.

events.name: Start of the Vikrama Samvat era
events.summary: Era reckoned from 57 BCE, traditionally linked to a king Vikramaditya of Ujjain.
events.note: The era's origin is debated; its starting year is fixed.

events.name: Start of the Shaka era
events.summary: Era beginning in 78 CE; later adopted for India's national calendar.
events.note: Traditionally linked to Kanishka; the link is contested.

events.name: Accession of Kanishka
events.summary: Leading Kushana ruler; patron of Buddhism and of the Gandhara and Mathura schools of art.
events.note: Older view 78 CE (Shaka era); many scholars now prefer c. 127 CE.

events.name: Reign of Gautamiputra Satakarni
events.summary: Satavahana ruler who defeated the Kshaharata Shaka Nahapana (Nasik inscription).
events.note: Chronologies vary.

events.name: Junagadh (Girnar) inscription of Rudradaman
events.summary: Early long Sanskrit inscription; records repair of the Sudarshana lake.
events.note: Dated Shaka year 72.

events.name: Sangam age
events.summary: Age of early Tamil poetry and the Chera, Chola and Pandya chiefdoms.
events.note: Ranges differ widely between scholars.

events.name: Start of the Gupta era
events.summary: Gupta era begins in 319-320 CE, usually linked to Chandragupta I's accession.

events.name: Reign of Samudragupta
events.summary: Gupta expansion recorded in Harishena's Prayag (Allahabad) prashasti.

events.name: Reign of Chandragupta II
events.summary: Defeat of the Western Kshatrapas; height of Gupta power.

events.name: Faxian (Fa-Hien) travels to India
events.summary: Chinese Buddhist pilgrim whose account describes north India under Chandragupta II.
events.note: 399-414 spans the whole journey from and back to China.

events.name: Reign of Kumaragupta I
events.summary: Gupta ruler traditionally credited with founding the Nalanda mahavihara.

events.name: Reign of Skandagupta
events.summary: Repulsed early Huna attacks.

events.name: Aryabhata composes the Aryabhatiya
events.summary: Astronomical and mathematical treatise.

events.name: Defeat of the Huna ruler Mihirakula
events.summary: Yashodharman of Malwa claims victory over Mihirakula (Mandsaur inscription).

events.name: Reign of Harshavardhana
events.summary: Ruler of Thanesar and Kannauj, known from the Harshacharita and Xuanzang's account.

events.name: Xuanzang (Hiuen Tsang) in India
events.summary: Chinese pilgrim who studied at Nalanda and attended Harsha's assemblies.

events.name: Pulakeshin II stops Harsha on the Narmada
events.summary: Chalukya victory over Harsha, recorded in the Aihole inscription.
events.note: Dated c. 618-619 or c. 630-634 CE in different works.

events.name: Aihole inscription of Pulakeshin II
events.summary: Prashasti by Ravikirti recording Pulakeshin II's victories.
events.note: Dated Shaka 556.

events.name: Pallava capture of Vatapi
events.summary: Pallava king Narasimhavarman I sacks the Chalukya capital; Pulakeshin II dies.

events.name: Arab conquest of Sindh
events.summary: Umayyad general Muhammad bin Qasim defeats Dahir and conquers Sindh.
events.note: Campaign of 711-712.

events.name: Tripartite struggle for Kannauj
events.summary: Long contest between Palas, Gurjara-Pratiharas and Rashtrakutas for control of Kannauj.

events.name: Reign of Dharmapala
events.summary: Pala ruler of Bengal; founder of the Vikramashila mahavihara.

events.name: Kailasa temple at Ellora
events.summary: Rock-cut temple excavated under the Rashtrakuta king Krishna I.

events.name: Reign of Amoghavarsha I
events.summary: Long-reigning Rashtrakuta king; the Kannada work Kavirajamarga is associated with his court.

events.name: Reign of Mihira Bhoja
events.summary: Most powerful Gurjara-Pratihara ruler.

events.name: Reign of Rajaraja I
events.summary: Chola expansion; built the Brihadishvara temple at Thanjavur (completed c. 1010).

events.name: Reign of Rajendra I
events.summary: Expeditions to the Ganga valley and Srivijaya; new capital at Gangaikonda Cholapuram.

events.name: Raids of Mahmud of Ghazni
events.summary: Series of about seventeen raids into north India.

events.name: Mahmud's raid on Somnath
events.summary: Sack of the Somnath temple in Gujarat.

events.name: Alberuni's Kitab-ul-Hind
events.summary: Account of Indian society, science and religion.

events.name: First Battle of Tarain
events.summary: Prithviraj Chauhan defeats Muhammad of Ghur.

events.name: Second Battle of Tarain
events.summary: Muhammad of Ghur defeats Prithviraj; opens north India to Ghurid rule.

events.name: Battle of Chandawar
events.summary: Muhammad of Ghur defeats Jaichand of Kannauj.

events.name: Bakhtiyar Khalji's raid on Nadia
events.summary: Raid on the Sena capital that began Turkish rule in Bengal.
events.note: Dated c. 1202-1205 in different accounts.

events.name: Qutbuddin Aibak rules at Delhi
events.summary: After Muhammad of Ghur's death Aibak rules as the first sultan of Delhi.

events.name: Reign of Iltutmish
events.summary: Consolidated the Sultanate; received investiture from the Abbasid caliph.

events.name: Reign of Raziya
events.summary: Only woman ruler of the Delhi Sultanate.

events.name: Reign of Balban
events.summary: Stressed royal prestige and broke the power of the Turkish nobility (the Forty).

events.name: Khalji revolution
events.summary: The Khaljis replace the Ilbari Turks on the Delhi throne.

events.name: Reign of Alauddin Khalji
events.summary: Market control, revenue measures and campaigns in Gujarat, Rajasthan and the Deccan.

events.name: Alauddin captures Chittor
events.summary: Siege and capture of Chittor.

events.name: Malik Kafur's southern campaigns
events.summary: Campaigns against Warangal, Dwarasamudra and Madurai.

events.name: Reign of Muhammad bin Tughlaq
events.summary: Reign known for ambitious and controversial projects.

events.name: Capital moved to Daulatabad
events.summary: Shift of the capital, and many inhabitants, from Delhi to Daulatabad.

events.name: Token currency experiment
events.summary: Bronze tokens issued at par with silver; withdrawn after widespread forgery.

events.name: Ibn Battuta in India
events.summary: Moroccan traveller who served as qazi of Delhi; described India in his Rihla.

events.name: Foundation of Vijayanagara
events.summary: Founded by Harihara and Bukka of the Sangama dynasty.
events.note: 1336 is the traditional date.

events.name: Foundation of the Bahmani kingdom
events.summary: Revolt against Muhammad bin Tughlaq creates an independent Deccan sultanate.

events.name: Reign of Firoz Shah Tughlaq
events.summary: Canals, new towns, and jizya extended to Brahmins.

events.name: Timur sacks Delhi
events.summary: Timur's invasion and sack of Delhi.

events.name: Lodi dynasty
events.summary: Afghan dynasty ended by Babur at Panipat.

events.name: Reign of Krishnadevaraya
events.summary: Peak of Vijayanagara power; author of the Telugu Amuktamalyada.

events.name: Battle of Raichur
events.summary: Krishnadevaraya defeats the sultan of Bijapur.

events.name: First Battle of Panipat
events.summary: Babur defeats Ibrahim Lodi and founds Mughal rule.

events.name: Battle of Khanwa
events.summary: Babur defeats Rana Sanga's Rajput confederacy.
events.note: Day given as 16 or 17 March.

events.name: Sher Shah defeats Humayun (Chausa and Kannauj)
events.summary: Chausa (1539) and Kannauj (1540) drive Humayun out of India.

events.name: Reign of Sher Shah Suri
events.summary: Administrative and revenue reforms, the silver rupiya, road building.

events.name: Accession of Akbar
events.summary: Akbar is enthroned at Kalanaur after Humayun's death.

events.name: Second Battle of Panipat
events.summary: Mughal victory over Hemu.

events.name: Battle of Talikota (Rakshasa-Tangadi)
events.summary: Combined Deccan sultanates defeat Vijayanagara; the capital is sacked.
events.note: Day given as 23 or 26 January.

events.name: Mansabdari system organised
events.summary: Graded ranks for nobles and officials.
events.note: The dual zat/sawar rank is dated to the 1590s.

events.name: Ibadat Khana built at Fatehpur Sikri
events.summary: Hall for religious debate.

events.name: Battle of Haldighati
events.summary: Mughal forces under Man Singh fight Maharana Pratap.
events.note: Day given as 18 or 21 June.

events.name: Mahzar declaration
events.summary: Gives Akbar the final word on disputed religious questions.

events.name: Dahsala (zabt) revenue system
events.summary: Revenue assessed on ten-year averages of produce and prices.

events.name: Din-i-Ilahi (Tauhid-i-Ilahi)
events.summary: Discipleship order centred on the emperor.

events.name: Execution of Guru Arjan
events.summary: Fifth Sikh Guru, compiler of the Adi Granth, executed on Jahangir's orders.

events.name: Sir Thomas Roe at Jahangir's court
events.summary: English ambassador seeking trading privileges.

events.name: Battle of Samugarh
events.summary: Aurangzeb defeats Dara Shikoh in the war of succession.

events.name: Treaty of Purandar
events.summary: Shivaji cedes forts to the Mughals.

events.name: Battle of Saraighat
events.summary: Ahom victory over the Mughals on the Brahmaputra.

events.name: Coronation of Shivaji
events.summary: Shivaji crowned Chhatrapati at Raigad.

events.name: Execution of Guru Tegh Bahadur
events.summary: Ninth Sikh Guru executed at Delhi.

events.name: Founding of the Khalsa
events.summary: Founded at Anandpur.

events.name: Death of Aurangzeb
events.summary: Followed by succession wars and weakening central control.

events.name: Farrukhsiyar's farman to the English Company
events.summary: Grants the English Company duty-free trade in Bengal.

events.name: Baji Rao I as Peshwa
events.summary: Northward expansion of Maratha power.

events.name: Nizam-ul-Mulk wins at Shakar Kheda
events.summary: Leads to the autonomous state of Hyderabad.

events.name: Nadir Shah's invasion
events.summary: Mughal defeat at Karnal and sack of Delhi; the Peacock Throne is carried away.

events.name: Third Battle of Panipat
events.summary: Afghan victory over the Marathas.

events.name: Amir Khusrau
events.summary: Poet and musician at the Sultanate court; disciple of Nizamuddin Auliya.

events.name: Death of Nizamuddin Auliya
events.summary: Chishti Sufi of Delhi.

events.name: Kabir
events.summary: Nirguna bhakti poet of Banaras.
events.note: Traditional and uncertain dates.

events.name: Life of Guru Nanak
events.summary: Founder of Sikhism.

events.name: Chaitanya Mahaprabhu
events.summary: Leader of Gaudiya Vaishnavism in Bengal.

events.name: Vasco da Gama reaches Calicut
events.summary: Opens the sea route from Europe to India round the Cape.

events.name: Portuguese capture Goa
events.summary: Goa becomes the centre of the Portuguese Estado da India.

events.name: English East India Company chartered
events.summary: Royal charter to the London company trading to the East Indies.

events.name: English factory at Surat
events.summary: First permanent English factory in Mughal India.

events.name: Carnatic Wars
events.summary: Three Anglo-French wars in south India (1746-48, 1749-54, 1756-63).

events.name: Battle of Wandiwash
events.summary: Decisive British victory over the French.

events.name: Treaty of Allahabad and grant of the Diwani
events.summary: Company obtains the diwani of Bengal, Bihar and Orissa.

events.name: Dual government in Bengal
events.summary: Company held the diwani while the nizamat stayed nominally with the Nawab.

events.name: Regulating Act
events.summary: Governor of Bengal made Governor-General; Supreme Court at Calcutta.

events.name: Pitt's India Act
events.summary: Board of Control set up over the Company.

events.name: Treaty of Salbai
events.summary: Ends the First Anglo-Maratha War.

events.name: Permanent Settlement
events.summary: Land revenue fixed in perpetuity with zamindars in Bengal.

events.name: Subsidiary alliance system
events.summary: Hyderabad is the first to accept (1798).

events.name: Fall of Seringapatam; death of Tipu Sultan
Treaty of Bassein
events.summary: Peshwa accepts a subsidiary alliance; leads to the Second Anglo-Maratha War.

events.name: Anglo-Maratha Wars
events.summary: Three wars (1775-82, 1803-05, 1817-18); the Peshwaship is abolished in 1818.

events.name: Treaty of Amritsar
events.summary: Sutlej fixed as the eastern limit of Ranjit Singh's kingdom.

events.name: Charter Act of 1813
events.summary: Ends the Company's India trade monopoly (tea and China trade excepted); provides one lakh rupees a year for education.

events.name: Ryotwari settlement in Madras
events.summary: Settlement made directly with cultivators.
events.note: Experiments from 1792; general extension c. 1820.

events.name: Mahalwari settlement
events.summary: Village-community (mahal) settlement in the North-Western Provinces.

events.name: Charter Act of 1833
events.summary: Governor-General of Bengal becomes Governor-General of India; Company's commercial role ends.

events.name: Annexation of Punjab
events.summary: Follows the Second Anglo-Sikh War.

events.name: Annexations under the Doctrine of Lapse
events.summary: Satara (1848) first; Jhansi and Nagpur among others.

events.name: Charter Act of 1853
events.summary: Introduces open competition for the civil service.

events.name: Annexation of Awadh
events.summary: Annexed on grounds of misgovernment.

events.name: Universities of Calcutta, Bombay and Madras founded
Government of India Act 1858
aliases: Act for the Better Government of India
events.summary: Rule passes from the Company to the Crown.

events.name: Indigo revolt
events.summary: Bengal peasants refuse to grow indigo.

events.name: Muhammadan Anglo-Oriental school and college at Aligarh
events.summary: School opened 1875; college 1877.

events.name: Deccan riots
events.summary: Peasants attack moneylenders in Poona and Ahmednagar districts.

events.name: Vernacular Press Act
events.summary: Repealed in 1882.

events.name: Indian National Congress founded
aliases: founding of the Indian National Congress
events.summary: First session held at Bombay.

events.name: Boycott resolution at Calcutta Town Hall
events.summary: Formal launch of the Swadeshi movement.

events.name: Partition of Bengal takes effect
events.summary: Announced in July 1905.

events.name: All-India Muslim League founded
events.summary: Founded at Dacca.

events.name: Surat split
events.summary: Congress splits between Moderates and Extremists.

events.name: Morley-Minto Reforms (Indian Councils Act 1909)
events.summary: Introduces separate electorates for Muslims.

events.name: Delhi Durbar announces annulment of the partition
aliases: annulment of the partition of Bengal
events.summary: Annulment and transfer of the capital to Delhi announced.

events.name: Ghadar Party founded
events.summary: Founded in the United States.

events.name: Home Rule Leagues founded
events.summary: Tilak's league in April, Besant's in September.

events.name: Lucknow Pact
events.summary: Congress-League agreement; Congress accepts separate electorates.

events.name: Champaran satyagraha
events.summary: Against the tinkathia system on indigo plantations.

events.name: Montagu Declaration
events.summary: Announces the goal of progressive realisation of responsible government.

events.name: Kheda satyagraha and Ahmedabad mill strike
Rowlatt Act passed
events.summary: Allows detention without trial.

events.name: Government of India Act 1919
events.summary: Introduces dyarchy in the provinces.

events.name: Non-Cooperation Movement launched
events.summary: Endorsed at the Calcutta (September) and Nagpur (December) sessions of 1920.

events.name: Swaraj Party formed
events.summary: Formed after the Gaya session rejected council entry.
events.note: Commonly dated 1 January 1923; some works say late 1922-early 1923.

events.name: Vaikom satyagraha
events.summary: Agitation for access to roads around the Vaikom temple in Travancore.

events.name: Simon Commission arrives in India
events.summary: Appointed November 1927; boycotted because it had no Indian member.

events.name: Bombs thrown in the Central Legislative Assembly
First Round Table Conference
events.summary: Congress did not attend.

events.name: Execution of Bhagat Singh, Rajguru and Sukhdev
Second Round Table Conference
events.summary: Gandhi attends as the sole Congress representative.

events.name: Poona Pact
events.summary: Reserved seats for the depressed classes within joint electorates.

events.name: Government of India Act 1935
events.summary: Provincial autonomy and a proposed all-India federation.

events.name: Congress ministries in office
events.summary: Resigned in October-November 1939 in protest at India's entry into the war.

events.name: Lahore Resolution of the Muslim League
events.summary: Moved on 23 March, adopted on 24 March.

events.name: Cripps Mission in India
events.summary: Offers post-war Dominion Status with the right to secede and a right for provinces not to join the new Union; rejected by both Congress and the League.
events.note: Arrived in Delhi 22 March (some sources say 23 March); left 11 or 12 April.

events.name: Cripps draft declaration published
events.note: Handed to the press on 29 March and published on 30 March.

events.name: Quit India resolution
events.summary: Passed at Bombay; leaders arrested on 9 August.

events.name: Provisional Government of Free India (Azad Hind)
Simla Conference on the Wavell Plan
events.summary: Broke down over the League's claim to nominate all Muslim members.

events.name: INA trials at the Red Fort
Royal Indian Navy mutiny
events.summary: Began in Bombay.

events.name: Cabinet Mission arrives in India
events.summary: Three-member British Cabinet delegation.

events.name: Second Simla Conference (tripartite talks)
events.summary: Talks between the Mission, Congress and the League end without agreement.

events.name: Cabinet Mission Plan (statement of 16 May)
events.summary: Three-tier union with provinces grouped into Sections A, B and C; Constituent Assembly elected by provincial assemblies; a sovereign Pakistan rejected.

events.name: Cabinet Mission statement of 25 May
events.summary: Calls grouping an essential feature of the scheme; says the Congress reading of paragraph 15 does not accord with the Mission's intentions.

events.name: Muslim League accepts the Plan
aliases: League acceptance of the Cabinet Mission Plan
events.summary: Accepts, holding that the basis of Pakistan is inherent in compulsory grouping.

events.name: Interim government proposals (16 June statement)
events.summary: Viceroy proposes a 14-member interim government.

events.name: Congress Working Committee resolution on the Plan
aliases: Congress acceptance of the Cabinet Mission Plan
events.summary: Accepts the 16 May long-term plan with its own reading of grouping; rejects the 16 June interim government proposals.

events.name: AICC ratifies the Working Committee's decision
Nehru's press conference on the Plan
events.summary: Says Congress is committed only to entering the Constituent Assembly and that there will probably be no grouping.

events.name: Muslim League withdraws its acceptance
aliases: League withdrawal from the Cabinet Mission Plan
events.summary: League Council withdraws acceptance and calls for Direct Action.

events.name: Direct Action Day and the Great Calcutta Killing
Interim Government headed by Nehru sworn in
Muslim League joins the Interim Government
events.summary: League nominees join; Liaquat Ali Khan takes Finance.
events.note: Sources give 25 or 26 October for the swearing-in; the decision to join came in mid-October.

events.name: British government statement of 6 December
events.summary: Upholds the Mission's reading that sections decide by majority; offers a Federal Court reference.

events.name: Constituent Assembly first meets
aliases: first session of the Constituent Assembly
events.summary: Meets without the Muslim League.

events.name: Objectives Resolution
events.summary: Moved on 13 December 1946, adopted on 22 January 1947.

events.name: Tebhaga movement
events.summary: Sharecroppers in Bengal demand two-thirds of the crop.

events.name: Indian Independence Act receives royal assent
Independence of India
events.summary: Pakistan's independence is dated 14 August.

events.name: Instrument of Accession of Jammu and Kashmir
Bhoodan movement begins
events.summary: Begins at Pochampally in Telangana.

events.name: Andhra State formed
events.summary: Follows Potti Sriramulu's death on fast in December 1952.

events.name: Glorious Revolution and Bill of Rights
events.summary: Parliament settles the Crown on William and Mary; the Bill of Rights limits royal power.

events.name: Locke's Two Treatises of Government
events.note: Published late 1689 with 1690 on the title page.

events.name: Montesquieu's The Spirit of the Laws
events.summary: Argues for separation of powers.

events.name: Spinning jenny
events.note: Invented c. 1764-65; patented 1770.

events.name: Stamp Act
events.summary: Colonial protest under the slogan of no taxation without representation.

events.name: Adam Smith's The Wealth of Nations
British surrender at Saratoga
events.summary: Leads to the French alliance of 1778.

events.name: Treaty of Paris (1783)
events.summary: Britain recognises American independence.

events.name: US Constitution signed
events.summary: In force from 1789.

events.name: Declaration of the Rights of Man and of the Citizen
aliases: Declaration of the Rights of Man

events.name: Grito de Dolores (Mexican independence struggle begins)
Battle of Leipzig (Battle of the Nations)
Congress of Vienna
events.summary: Final Act signed on 9 June 1815.

events.name: Treaty of Nanking
events.summary: Hong Kong ceded; treaty ports opened.

events.name: Revolutions of 1848
events.summary: Uprisings in France, the German states, the Habsburg lands and Italy.

events.name: Crimean War
events.summary: Ended by the Treaty of Paris, 30 March 1856.

events.name: Emancipation of the serfs in Russia
events.note: Dated 19 February 1861 in the Old Style calendar.

events.name: American Civil War begins at Fort Sumter
Triple Alliance
events.summary: Germany, Austria-Hungary and Italy.

events.name: First Sino-Japanese War
events.summary: Ended by the Treaty of Shimonoseki, 17 April 1895.

events.name: Boxer Rebellion
events.summary: Ended by the Boxer Protocol, 7 September 1901.

events.name: Russo-Japanese War
events.summary: Ended by the Treaty of Portsmouth, 5 September 1905.

events.name: Bloody Sunday, start of the 1905 Revolution
events.note: 9 January in the Old Style calendar.

events.name: Moroccan crises
events.summary: Tangier (1905) and Agadir (1911).

events.name: Austria-Hungary declares war on Serbia
aliases: outbreak of the First World War

events.name: February Revolution in Russia
events.note: 23-27 February in the Old Style calendar.

events.name: United States enters the First World War
aliases: US entry into the First World War

events.name: October Revolution (Bolshevik seizure of power)
events.note: 25 October in the Old Style calendar.

events.name: Armistice ends the First World War
League of Nations comes into being
Munich Agreement
events.note: Signed in the early hours of 30 September; dated 29 September.

events.name: Britain and France declare war on Germany
aliases: outbreak of the Second World War

events.name: Battle of Stalingrad
events.summary: German surrender on 2 February 1943.

events.name: UN Charter signed at San Francisco
Indonesian independence proclaimed
events.summary: Dutch recognition followed on 27 December 1949.

events.name: Japan signs the instrument of surrender
National Party victory; apartheid policy begins
Treaty of Paris creates the ECSC
Geneva Accords on Indochina
events.summary: Vietnam divided at the 17th parallel.

events.name: Nasser nationalises the Suez Canal Company
Treaty of Rome (EEC)
events.summary: EEC in operation from 1 January 1958.

events.name: Great Leap Forward
events.note: Some works date its end to 1961-62.

events.name: Year of Africa
events.summary: Seventeen African states become independent.

events.name: Maastricht Treaty signed
events.summary: In force from 1 November 1993.

events.name: Euro introduced
events.summary: Notes and coins from 1 January 2002.

names: Chandragupta Maurya founds the Mauryan empire
War and treaty with Seleucus Nicator
Start of the Vikrama Samvat era
Defeat of the Huna ruler Mihirakula
Pulakeshin II stops Harsha on the Narmada
Sher Shah defeats Humayun (Chausa and Kannauj)
Sir Thomas Roe at Jahangir's court
